findings.message:
[P1] Legacy cookie check locks out existing sessions

`hubSessionToken` now returns an empty token whenever *any* `dua_session` cookie is present, but this change only writes or clears `__Host-dua_session`. Every user signed in before this deploy still carries the old host-only `dua_session` cookie (30-day TTL), and neither login nor logout ever removes it, so after a successful login the browser keeps sending the legacy cookie and `/api/auth/session/me`, admin, and SSO requests remain unauthenticated until it expires or the user manually clears cookies (up to 30 days). Clear the legacy cookie during login/logout migration while still rejecting genuinely ambiguous pairs.

src/session_cookie.ts:35-37

[P2] Plain-HTTP guard breaks documented localhost development

`hubSessionCookie` and `clearHubSessionCookie` now return an empty string for every non-HTTPS request. `deno task dev` serves at `http://localhost:8000`, so password and passkey login no longer set a session cookie and the UI cannot stay signed in locally (the frontend relies on the cookie rather than the returned bearer token). The acceptance criterion targets the production cookie over plaintext HTTP; scope the refusal to non-loopback hosts so the documented local flow keeps working.

src/session_cookie.ts:45-45

summary: The cookie is renamed to __Host-dua_session with Secure/Path and duplicates are rejected, but the unconditional legacy-cookie rejection locks out all pre-existing sessions because the old cookie is never cleared, and the plaintext guard breaks the documented localhost dev flow.

evidence: src/session_cookie.ts switches to a __Host-dua_session cookie with Secure, Path=/ and no Domain, and refuses to issue it over plaintext.
src/session_cookie.ts rejects duplicate __Host-dua_session values and any legacy dua_session cookie.
tests/worker_runtime.mjs only injects a literal Cookie header into workerd; no browser-level sibling-domain regression exists.
The unconditional legacy rejection is never accompanied by clearing the old cookie on login/logout, so existing browser sessions are locked out for up to 30 days.
